The adjudication merely bars a second action relitigating the same alleged default. The court continued stating that it agreed with the analysis of the Middle District of Florida court in Dorta that where a mortgage foreclosures action is unsuccessful for whatever reason, the mortgagee still has the right to file later foreclosure actions so long as they are based on separate defaults. In Bartram, the court continued whether the dismissal of the initial foreclosure action by the court was with or without prejudice may be relevant to the mortgagee's ability to collect on past defaults. However, each subsequent default accruing after the dismissal of an earlier foreclosure action creates a new cause of action regardless of whether that dismissal was entered with or without prejudice. And one last point from Bartram, the court held as we cautioned in Singleton, justice would not be served if the mortgagee was barred from challenging the subsequent default payment solely because he failed to prove the earlier alleged default. Foreclosure is a proceeding in equity and the two defenses raised here on appeal, although not as the court pointed out and not below, of res judicata and collateral estoppel are defenses that arise only in equity.
